title: Carnival, Indians and a parade Cahn attended that day
summary: Cahn says tribes would not exist without Carnival and describes a large parade of four groups in matching colors that he watched earlier that day.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: We were going to try and get into, do you see any direct influence on any popular music? I brought a few selections.
I'm not a, I'm not much on popular music, as you would call it, on your rock and so forth. Yeah. I've tried to tune it out.

Well, I can see that. No, I was more thinking of music here in New Orleans. And what do you see the influence between Carnival and the Indians? Without Carnival, do you think there would be an Indian group? There would be tribes? In other words?

No. There wouldn't be tribes. However, they might come into a, into something different, because just today you had a, a very large parade actually composed of four bands in which the members of the organization, the organization being the scene highlighters, which they dressed up, but in a, one group was in the yellow, and they, it was very, very interesting, because they had ostrich plume fans, and, and very exotic shoes, which seems to be a large part of the culture, the shoes, and, some were in green, some were in yellow, and some were in rows, and different groups in which they marched down the street. the parade started at, 11 this morning, and I left it at about four, and they still had over an hour to go.
They started on, Arlene's, and, Dupree, or Dersion, and they were going to end on Louisiana Avenue, and, South Liberty. That's the route.
Mm-hmm. That's a pretty good march.
but they don't go straight. Yeah. They go through the neighborhoods.
